boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented DePauw rituals spanning arrival, rivalry, spring racing, senior honors and the final walk across campus.

cards.title: Play for a 300-Pound Railroad Bell
cards.subtitle: DePauw and Wabash’s annual football rivalry
cards.notes: Watch for the locomotive bell beside the field; the winning school keeps the 300-pound trophy until the rivals meet again.
cards.short_summary: A nearby college rivalry decides which campus houses an actual railroad bell for the next year.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw and Wabash have played football since 1890 and have competed for possession of the 300-pound Monon Railroad bell since 1932.
cards.access_notes: Game location and admission arrangements vary by year; consult the current university athletics or alumni announcement before attending.

cards.title: Turn Campus Streets Into a Bike Course
cards.subtitle: DePauw’s spring cycling week since 1956
cards.notes: Follow the time trial, street sprints and final criterium; use designated spectator areas and leave the closed course to registered racers.
cards.short_summary: A fundraiser-born bicycle race has evolved into a week of racing and spring events around campus.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw’s Little 5 has been held since 1956 and currently progresses from a time trial to street sprints and criterium races on a half-mile campus course.
cards.access_notes: Held in late April; current routes, road closures and spectator instructions should be confirmed through DePauw event notices.

cards.title: Replace Class Scraps With Old Gold
cards.subtitle: A homecoming tradition created in 1907
cards.notes: Check the weekend program for the football game, arts events and alumni gatherings—the modern, organized successors to early class contests.
cards.short_summary: DePauw transformed unruly class rivalries into a structured homecoming celebration more than a century ago.
cards.evidence_claim: Old Gold Day began in 1907 to replace increasingly violent freshman-sophomore contests and had developed into a full homecoming weekend by 1919.
cards.access_notes: The university schedules Old Gold Weekend annually; individual activities may have separate registration or access requirements.

cards.title: Enter DePauw Through the East College Gates
cards.subtitle: The new-student welcome march across campus
cards.notes: Join the procession with your residence mentor and pass through the gates; bring ear protection if cheering and amplified sound feel overwhelming.
cards.short_summary: New Tigers symbolically enter the university together before their welcome convocation.
cards.evidence_claim: During orientation, new students process across campus with residence assistants and mentors and walk through the East College gates as their official welcome into the DePauw community.
cards.access_notes: Designed for incoming students and families during orientation; the procession includes loud music, cheering and clapping, with a quiet room available.

cards.title: Leave Through the Same Historic Arch
cards.subtitle: A ceremonial bookend to the opening-week march
cards.notes: Notice the DPU letters overhead as the graduating procession crosses the historic arch—the ceremonial counterpart to the first-year entrance.
cards.short_summary: DePauw uses its historic campus gateway to frame both arrival and graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw identifies the ornamental DPU Arch as an essential pass-through for both the opening-week march and commencement ceremonies.
cards.access_notes: Participation is tied to official commencement instructions; graduates should follow the University Marshal’s procession guidance.

cards.title: Sing a Toast Written by an Alumna
cards.subtitle: DePauw’s ceremonial university anthem
cards.notes: Listen for Vivien Bard’s anthem at formal gatherings; follow the printed program when the community joins in the school-specific song.
cards.short_summary: An alumna’s composition supplies the shared song for DePauw ceremonies and reunions.
cards.evidence_claim: Vivien Bard’s “A Toast to Old DePauw” became the official university anthem and has been sung at commencement, Old Gold Day, Alumni Day and other ceremonies.
cards.access_notes: Performed as part of selected university ceremonies; attendance conditions depend on the host event.

cards.title: Let Seniors Choose a Cup Winner
cards.subtitle: An annual student honor established in 1926
cards.notes: Attend the Student Awards Convocation to see the cup presented after senior-class nominations recognize service to the university.
cards.short_summary: Graduating students help select the classmate whose contribution to DePauw is commemorated by a historic cup.
cards.evidence_claim: Established in 1926, the Walker Cup is presented annually to a graduating senior nominated by the senior class for exceptional contribution to DePauw.
cards.source_title: Outstanding Seniors Honored with Walker Cup and Murad Medal
cards.access_notes: Presented during the annual Student Awards Convocation; verify the current ceremony’s venue and attendance guidance.

cards.title: Meet at the Campus’s Giant Granite Marker
cards.subtitle: A gathering custom on the East College lawn
cards.notes: Use the inscribed Boulder as a daylight meeting point and examine it from the lawn; avoid the unsafe, clothing-optional run in older lore.
cards.short_summary: A granite curiosity delivered by 26 horses became a long-running campus rendezvous point.
cards.evidence_claim: The Columbian Boulder has served as an iconic student gathering place, and DePauw’s archives document its earlier use as a meeting point for chapel dates.
cards.access_notes: Viewable outdoors on the East College lawn; this card covers the safe gathering custom and explicitly excludes the Boulder Run.

cards.title: Begin Commencement With Many Traditions
cards.subtitle: DePauw’s formal ceremony before graduation day
cards.notes: Arrive before the listed start to hear student reflections, music, prayers and readings that open DePauw’s commencement weekend.
cards.short_summary: Graduation weekend formally begins with a multi-tradition gathering centered on the senior class.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw describes Baccalaureate as the first formal event of Commencement Weekend, featuring the president, student reflections, music, prayers and readings from many traditions.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 ceremony was scheduled in Kresge Auditorium and required no tickets; future dates and access should be reconfirmed.

cards.title: Gather Under the Stars Before Graduation
cards.subtitle: A named commencement-weekend evening event
cards.notes: Join graduates and guests at Stewart Plaza for the scheduled music and conversation; check the rain location before setting out.
cards.short_summary: DePauw gives seniors and their guests a relaxed outdoor evening between Baccalaureate and Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: The university’s 2026 Commencement schedule included “DePauw Under the Stars,” an evening of music and conversation for graduates, families and guests at Stewart Plaza.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for commencement weekend at Stewart Plaza, with Hoover Hall and the Union Building Living Room listed as inclement-weather locations.
